cluster.headline: Bihar floods widen as Ganga sets record level at Bhagalpur gauge
cluster.summary: Bihar's Disaster Management Department reported the Ganga at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur reading 36.80 metres at 8 am on 8 September, above the previous record of 36.75 metres from 17 August 2021, with more than 34 lakh people affected. Earlier copy in the week counted 19.57 lakh people in 330 gram panchayats across 11 districts, rising to 22 lakh across 14 districts, with the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and Ganga running high.

story.headline: Ganga reported at record level in Bhagalpur as Bihar flood toll widens
story.body:
The Ganga at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur was recorded at 36.80 metres at 8 am on 8 September, according to figures attributed to Bihar's Disaster Management Department in the intake note for this story. That reading is described as being above the previous high of 36.75 metres, logged on 17 August 2021.

The same departmental figures put the number of people affected by flooding in the state at more than 34 lakh. The intake note does not break that total down by district, nor does it specify how the department counts an affected person.

Earlier reporting during the week, as summarised in the intake note, gave lower and rising counts: 19.57 lakh people across 330 gram panchayats in 11 districts, then 22 lakh people across 14 districts. The Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and Ganga were all described as running high.

No wire copy has been located for this brief. The intake note flags PTI-datelined material from 6 September and a freshest wire item roughly 19 hours old, but neither has been read or verified for this draft, and no quotes or on-the-record comments are available.

This is a working draft and not for publication as it stands. Before it runs, the desk needs to obtain the Disaster Management Department bulletin directly and confirm the 36.80-metre reading, the record-comparison claim and the 34 lakh affected figure; establish a district-wise breakdown and current warning levels for the four rivers; check whether there are casualties, displacement or relief-camp numbers, none of which appear in the intake note; and pull the original PTI copy. Whether river levels have since risen or receded is not confirmed.

blocks.label: Headline
lines: भागलपुर में गंगा रिकॉर्ड स्तर पर, बिहार में बाढ़ की मार का दायरा बढ़ा

blocks.label: Body
lines: इस समाचार की इनटेक नोट में बिहार के आपदा प्रबंधन विभाग के हवाले से दिए गए आंकड़ों के अनुसार, भागलपुर के सुल्तानगंज में गंगा नदी का जलस्तर 8 सितंबर को सुबह 8 बजे 36.80 मीटर दर्ज किया गया। बताया गया है कि यह स्तर 17 अगस्त 2021 को दर्ज किए गए पिछले उच्चतम स्तर 36.75 मीटर से अधिक है।

विभाग के इन्हीं आंकड़ों में राज्य में बाढ़ से प्रभावित लोगों की संख्या 34 लाख से अधिक बताई गई है। इनटेक नोट में इस कुल संख्या का जिलेवार ब्योरा नहीं है, और न ही यह स्पष्ट किया गया है कि विभाग किसे प्रभावित व्यक्ति के रूप में गिनता है।

इनटेक नोट में संकलित सप्ताह के दौरान की पिछली रिपोर्टिंग में इससे कम, लेकिन लगातार बढ़ती संख्याएं दी गई थीं: 11 जिलों के 330 ग्राम पंचायतों में 19.57 लाख लोग, और उसके बाद 14 जिलों में 22 लाख लोग। गंडक, कोसी, बूढ़ी गंडक और गंगा — सभी नदियों का जलस्तर ऊंचा बताया गया था।

इस ब्रीफ के लिए कोई वायर कॉपी नहीं मिली है। इनटेक नोट में 6 सितंबर की पीटीआई-डेटलाइन वाली सामग्री और लगभग 19 घंटे पुरानी सबसे ताज़ा वायर खबर का उल्लेख है, लेकिन इस ड्राफ्ट के लिए इनमें से किसी को पढ़ा या सत्यापित नहीं किया गया है, और न ही कोई उद्धरण या ऑन-द-रिकॉर्ड टिप्पणी उपलब्ध है।

यह एक कार्यकारी ड्राफ्ट है और मौजूदा स्वरूप में प्रकाशन के लिए नहीं है। इसे चलाने से पहले डेस्क को आपदा प्रबंधन विभाग का बुलेटिन सीधे प्राप्त करना होगा और 36.80 मीटर के जलस्तर, रिकॉर्ड-तुलना के दावे तथा 34 लाख प्रभावितों के आंकड़े की पुष्टि करनी होगी; चारों नदियों के लिए जिलेवार ब्योरा और मौजूदा चेतावनी स्तर स्थापित करने होंगे; यह जांचना होगा कि मृतकों, विस्थापन या राहत शिविरों से जुड़े कोई आंकड़े हैं या नहीं, जिनमें से कोई भी इनटेक नोट में मौजूद नहीं है; और मूल पीटीआई कॉपी निकालनी होगी। नदियों का जलस्तर उसके बाद बढ़ा है या घटा, इसकी पुष्टि नहीं हुई है।

In the mid-ground, a small wooden country boat with a peeling blue hull is tethered to a partially submerged temple plinth; three Indian men in their thirties and forties — one in a checked lungi and faded vest, one in a plain grey kurta, one in a soaked polo shirt with trousers rolled to the knee — stand on the highest dry step watching the water, natural skin tones, realistic sweat, wet hair, unposed body language, one shielding his eyes with his hand. imagePrompts: Vertical 9:16 photojournalistic frame, shot on a Canon EOS R5 with 35mm f/1.8 lens, late afternoon overcast light in Bihar during monsoon. Wide elevated view from a raised embankment road in Bhagalpur: swollen brown floodwater of the Ganga stretching to the horizon, half-submerged banana and paddy fields, treetops and a small submerged brick shrine breaking the water surface, distant partially flooded village rooftops. In the mid-ground, a wooden country boat poled by two men in mud-stained lungis and faded shirts ferries a family — a woman in a wet cotton saree holding a bundle of clothes, a teenage boy clutching a plastic drum, an elderly man in a white kurta — realistic Indian faces with visible sweat, damp hair, natural skin texture and imperfections, tired but composed expressions. On the embankment edge left of frame, villagers squat beside tarpaulin sheets, cycles and aluminium pots, a stray dog and a soaked bundle of hay; a battered auto-rickshaw and a hand-painted local shop shutter visible at the far left edge. Muted monsoon palette: silty ochre-brown water, grey-white clouds, desaturated greens, damp concrete grey; soft diffused light, no harsh highlights, slight lens haze and a few water droplets, authentic film-like grain, natural depth of field with sharp mid-ground and gently soft distance. Bottom third of the frame kept calm and open — flat expanse of dark rippling floodwater in shadow, uncluttered, no subjects, leaving clean space for a caption. brief.headline: Ganga reported at record level in Bhagalpur as Bihar flood toll widens
brief.body:
The Ganga at Sultanganj in Bhagalpur was recorded at 36.80 metres at 8 am on 8 September, according to figures attributed to Bihar's Disaster Management Department in the intake note for this story. That reading is described as being above the previous high of 36.75 metres, logged on 17 August 2021.

The same departmental figures put the number of people affected by flooding in the state at more than 34 lakh. The intake note does not break that total down by district, nor does it specify how the department counts an affected person.

Earlier reporting during the week, as summarised in the intake note, gave lower and rising counts: 19.57 lakh people across 330 gram panchayats in 11 districts, then 22 lakh people across 14 districts. The Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak and Ganga were all described as running high.

No wire copy has been located for this brief. The intake note flags PTI-datelined material from 6 September and a freshest wire item roughly 19 hours old, but neither has been read or verified for this draft, and no quotes or on-the-record comments are available.

This is a working draft and not for publication as it stands. Before it runs, the desk needs to obtain the Disaster Management Department bulletin directly and confirm the 36.80-metre reading, the record-comparison claim and the 34 lakh affected figure; establish a district-wise breakdown and current warning levels for the four rivers; check whether there are casualties, displacement or relief-camp numbers, none of which appear in the intake note; and pull the original PTI copy. Whether river levels have since risen or receded is not confirmed.
